scenarios.name: Noisy Romanian botnet credential stuffing
scenarios.description: Cheap high-volume stuffing from Romanian hosting with an unusual Chrome build, many failures per account in rapid succession from a small shared IP pool.
scenarios.rationale: Meant to trigger nearly everything: new country, new ASN, new /24 and IP, new browser+OS+device, high likelihood-ratio scores for IP/ASN/country/browser, high failure velocity per account, many distinct accounts per IP/range/ASN, high threat-list share, and takeover history from the ASN and IPs. Serves as the baseline easy case matching the training campaign.

scenarios.name: Same-ASN same-device low and slow
scenarios.description: Attacker with stolen session fingerprint data logs in from a new IP inside the victim's usual /24 on their own ISP, copying their browser/OS/device, at the victim's usual hours, with no or one failed attempt.
scenarios.rationale: Designed to evade novelty signals (country, ASN, and /24 all known; only IP is new), likelihood-ratio scores (matches the victim's own history rather than attack traffic), device novelty (mimic), time-of-day anomalies, and velocity (at most one failure, long gaps). Also avoids shared-infrastructure counts since each IP is used once and by one account, and has no threat list or takeover history. Only the new IP remains as a weak signal.

scenarios.name: Norwegian residential proxy blend-in
scenarios.description: Attacker rents residential proxies in Norway on popular local ISPs, uses a fresh IP per attempt and a very common browser/OS combo, with a few failures spaced out over hours.
scenarios.rationale: Evades country novelty and country likelihood ratio by staying in Norway, evades ASN popularity/rarity and ASN threat-share by using a high-share local ASN, dilutes per-IP and per-/24 shared-infrastructure counts via fresh IPs, and avoids takeover history on IPs. Browser+OS is popular so popularity and likelihood signals are weak. Still leaves new ASN/IP/device novelty for the account, some failure velocity, and possibly a device change signal.

scenarios.name: Rented server night-time spray from Germany
scenarios.description: Medium-skill attacker using a small rented-server ASN in Germany with a handful of reused IPs, an outdated Firefox on Linux, attacking at night with moderate failures per account.
scenarios.rationale: Triggers new country and rare ASN novelty, high ASN likelihood ratio and low ASN popularity, unusual browser+OS combo, night-time timing, and shared-IP signals (many accounts per IP and per ASN in 24h). Moderate gap between attempts keeps per-minute failure velocity low, testing whether hourly and 24h velocity and shared infrastructure still catch it. IPs are not yet on threat lists, testing detection without threat intelligence.

scenarios.name: Careful foreign mobile-mimic with fresh IPs
scenarios.description: Patient attacker from the Netherlands on a popular local ISP there, fresh IP per attempt, using a common mobile device profile, one failed attempt, with hours between tries at random times.
scenarios.rationale: Evades shared-infrastructure counts (each IP used once), threat intelligence (clean IPs on a mainstream ASN), takeover history, and failure velocity (very long gaps, one failure), and keeps browser+OS popularity high. Still exposes new country, new ASN and IP novelty and a country likelihood ratio, testing whether novelty alone is enough when everything else looks benign. Differs from the Norwegian blend-in by crossing a border and using mobile.
